key_cases.case_name: Miles v. Child Protective Services Department
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of claims arising from an emergency removal, holding the caseworker was entitled to the good-faith immunity of RCW 26.44.056(3) where she relied on the opinions of treating physicians, and that the parents identified no clearly established constitutional right to support their section 1983 claim.
key_cases.relevance: The removal rested on the diagnoses of hospital physicians, and reliance on those medical opinions supported the caseworker's good faith.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that a rational trier could not find causation, and that a rational trier would be obligated to find good faith.

key_cases.case_name: M.W. v. Department of Social & Health Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that the implied negligent-investigation action under RCW 26.44.050 is a narrow exception limited to biased or faulty investigations producing a harmful placement decision, and does not reach other investigative harms such as an intrusive physical examination of the child.
key_cases.relevance: The claimed harm arose from investigators' physical examination of the child, and the court held that such investigative harm is outside the statutory cause of action.
key_cases.quote: such a claim is available only when DSHS conducts a biased or faulty investigation that leads to a harmful placement decision
